newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to expand its oil pipeline network - official.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to expand its oil pipeline network - official.

text.p: Iraq plans to expand its oil pipeline links with its neighbours in order to increase its oil export capacity, Iraqi newspapers quoted a senior oil official as saying on Tuesday.

"The (oil) ministry is planning in the future to expand its oil exports pipeline networks via neighbouring countries in order to guarantee the flow of Iraqi oil and increase its oil export capacities," said oil undersecretary Sami Shareef in remarks published by the official al-Qadissiya.
Shareef said French, Chinese and Russian firms "expressed their readiness to develop some oilfields which would increase Iraq's export capacities."
"Talks with these firms have reached good stages," he said adding that Baghdad plans to increase its export capacity to six million barrels per day (bpd).
Iraq started on December 10 limited oil sales under an oil- for-food deal signed with the United Nations which is imposing a ban on Baghdad's oil exports for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Under the deal, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food and medicine for the Iraqi population.

Under current oil prices, Baghdad is permitted to export 650,000 barrels per day through its oil pipeline via Turkey and Mina al-Bakr terminal in the Gulf. A further pipeline through Saudi Arabia has been closed since the Gulf War.
Iraqi officials have repeatedly said that their oil facilities are able to handle more that amount. Prior to U.N. sanctions Iraq exported more than 2.5 million bpd, up to 1.5 million through Turkey.
"Iraq's proven oil reserve is around 112 billion barrels which could be increased to 214 billion barrels," Qadissiya said.
